title: stable-diffusion.cpp .ckpt loader -- T1059 SHORT_BINUNICODE sign confusion causes heap corruption
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-47749 (GHSA-2c29-5hxg-fv9g,
CVSS 7.8 HIGH), affecting stable-diffusion.cpp prior to
master-584-0a7ae07.

The pickle `.ckpt` parser in `src/model.cpp` handles the
`SHORT_BINUNICODE` opcode's length field with a SIGN CONFUSION bug: the
length is read as if unsigned but the underlying storage permits a
negative signed value, which a crafted `.ckpt` file can supply. That
negative-interpreted-as-huge length is passed directly to `memcpy`,
causing immediate heap corruption -- a process crash at minimum, with
the advisory noting potential for code execution depending on heap
layout. Any application loading untrusted `.ckpt` checkpoint files
through affected stable-diffusion.cpp releases is exposed; the
advisory's own workaround (pending upgrade) is to load only trusted
`.safetensors` files instead of `.ckpt`, since `.safetensors` has no
pickle-based parsing path to exploit.

Detection logic flags a `.ckpt` model file whose SHORT_BINUNICODE
opcode (byte value `0x8c` in the pickle protocol) is immediately
followed by a length byte with its high bit set -- the specific
bit pattern that a correctly-signed parser would reject as invalid but
the vulnerable sign-confused one accepts and forwards to `memcpy`.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (leejet, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact source file, opcode name, and root
cause), fixed in master-584-0a7ae07.
